<user_input>ROLES:
Ethan: Neil Armstrong (Commander, first human to walk on the Moon)
Lily: Buzz Aldrin (Lunar Module Pilot, second to walk on the Moon)
James: Michael Collins (Command Module Pilot, orbits the Moon alone in Columbia)

The story takes place in July 1969, beginning at Kennedy Space Center in Florida, continuing through three days of space travel, and ending on the surface of the Moon at the Sea of Tranquility, with parallel scenes at Mission Control in Houston where Rachel and Margaret watch from the ground. Before the launch, Margaret tells Ethan and Lily that she has waited her whole life to see humans leave Earth and reach the Moon, and she gives Ethan a folded piece of paper with President Kennedy's 1961 promise written on it, which Ethan puts in his pocket. On 16th July 1969, Ethan, Lily, and James launch from Kennedy Space Center aboard the Saturn V rocket while Rachel and Margaret watch the lift-off from Mission Control in Houston, where Rachel works as part of the support team relaying data between the crew and the flight director. During the three-day journey, Ethan wanders into a section of the spacecraft he has been told not to enter and Lily skips a step in the equipment checklist, and James — orbiting alone in Columbia while they prepare the Eagle — catches both mistakes over the radio and guides them back to the correct procedure before the descent begins. As the Eagle descends toward the Moon, the 1202 alarm sounds, and Ethan takes manual control while Lily reads the fuel gauge aloud, counting down the seconds, and Rachel in Houston passes the flight director's instructions through her radio station to the crew without pausing. Ethan lands the Eagle with fewer than thirty seconds of fuel remaining, and at Mission Control, Rachel stands up from her station and Margaret grips the back of her chair, the two of them watching the same screen in the same room for the first time during the mission. Ethan steps out first onto the surface of the Moon, reads Kennedy's promise from the folded paper in his pocket, then puts it away and speaks his words into the radio. Lily follows him out, and together they plant the American flag — held open by a wire so it does not fall in the airless silence — collect rock samples, and read the plaque aloud before returning to the Eagle, their voices carrying the 1.3-second delay back to Margaret's ears in Houston.</user_input>
